title: The Sound of Music
tagline: Seven children, one whistle, and nobody leaves the table hungry.
about: A young postulant from a Salzburg abbey becomes governess to a widowed naval captain's seven children in 1938 Austria.
cue: Serve the main when Maria sits down to her first dinner with the von Trapp children.
faces: is requested for dinner and a film at
SALZBURG, AUSTRIA. PARTY NIGHT AT THE VILLA.
Seven children, one whistle, and nobody leaves the table hungry.
The Captain wants everyone at the table by seven. Napkins on laps, no pine cones on the chairs, and whoever let the frog into the pantry can fetch it back out.
Whipped quark and butter with paprika, caraway, capers and chives, with dark rye.
NONNBERG ABBEY PRETZELS WITH SWEET MUSTARD
Soft baked pretzels with a dark chewy crust and salt flakes, with sweet mustard for dipping.
Browned cheese kranskys with caraway sauerkraut, horseradish cream, hot mustard and cornichons.
Seated near: Play clothes cut from the old bedroom curtains
Showtime: Serve the main when Maria sits down to her first dinner with the von Trapp children. Also on the list: The Captain's bosun's whistle. All drinks alcohol free.

sweet paprika, plus extra to dust1 tsp caraway seeds, crushed1 tsp mustard1 tbsp capers, chopped1 eschalot, finely chopped2 tbsp chives, choppedsalt, to taste8 slices of dark rye bread1 bunch radishes, halved8 gherkinsBeat the quark and butter together until smooth.Stir in the paprika, caraway, mustard, capers, eschalot, chives and salt.Cover and chill until firm.Pile into a bowl, dust with paprika and serve with the rye bread, radishes and gherkins.Nonnberg Abbey pretzels with sweet mustardSoft baked pretzels with a dark chewy crust and salt flakes, with sweet mustard for dippingHow to make it500g bread flour7g dried yeast1 tsp sugar1 1/2 tsp salt40g butter, softened300ml warm water2 L water, for the bath4 tbsp bicarbonate of soda2 tsp salt flakes125ml sweet mustardMix the flour, yeast, sugar, salt, butter and warm water, then knead until smooth and elastic.Cover and prove until doubled.Cut into 8 pieces, roll each into a 50cm rope, thin at the ends, and twist into pretzels.Rest on lined trays.Simmer the bath water with the bicarbonate of soda and dip each pretzel for 30 seconds, then put back on the trays.Sprinkle with salt flakes, slash the thick part and bake at 220°C until deep brown.Cool a few minutes and serve warm with sweet mustard.Uncle Max's cheese kransky boardBrowned cheese kranskys with caraway sauerkraut, horseradish cream, hot mustard and a splash of water.Score the kranskys and brown in the oil over medium heat, turning, until the cheese bubbles out.Slice on an angle.Pile on a board with the sauerkraut, horseradish cream, mustard and cornichons.MainsCaptain von Trapp's TafelspitzBeef rump cap simmered with root vegetables in its own broth, apple horseradish, chive sauce and buttered potatoesHow to make it1 brown onion, halved1.5kg beef rump cap3 L cold water2 carrots, in chunks1 leek, in chunks250g celeriac, in chunks2 bay leaves10 black peppercorns2 tsp salt800g waxy potatoes50g butter2 tbsp parsley, chopped2 green apples3 tbsp horseradish cream1/2 lemon, juiced200g sour cream2 tbsp mayonnaise1 tsp white wine vinegar1 bunch chives, choppedChar the onion cut side down in a dry pan until black.Put the beef in a large pot with the cold water, bring to a simmer and skim.Add the onion, carrots, leek, celeriac, bay leaves, peppercorns and salt and simmer very gently, lid ajar, until tender.Meanwhile boil the potatoes until just tender, drain and slice thickly.Grate the apples into the horseradish cream with the lemon juice.Mix the sour cream, mayonnaise, vinegar and chives with a pinch of salt.Fry the potatoes in the butter until golden and toss with the parsley.Rest the beef in the broth, slice across the grain and serve in shallow bowls with a ladle of broth, the potatoes and both sauces.Schnitzel with noodlesOne of Maria's favourite things. Veal crumbed thin, buttered noodlesHow to make it4 veal schnitzels, about 120g each60g plain flour2 eggs120g dried breadcrumbs120ml vegetable oil60g butter300g wide egg noodles1 small bunch parsley2 lemonsBeat the veal thin between baking paper, then dip in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs.Boil the noodles, drain and toss with half the butter, chopped parsley and salt.Fry the schnitzels in the oil and the rest of the butter, shaking the pan so the crumb puffs, until golden on both sides.Drain on paper and serve with the noodles and lemon wedges.SweetsSalzburger NockerlThree golden peaks of baked vanilla and lemon meringue souffle over warm raspberries, dusted with icing sugarHow to make it30g butter200g frozen raspberries120g caster sugar150ml milk1 tsp vanilla extract6 eggs, separatedpinch of salt1/2 lemon, zested30g plain flour, sifted1 tbsp icing sugarHeat the oven to 200°C. Butter the dish, add the raspberries, 2 tbsp of the sugar, the milk and half the vanilla and warm in the oven.Whisk the 6 egg whites with the salt to soft peaks, then whisk in the rest of the sugar a spoonful at a time until stiff and glossy.Mix 4 of the yolks with the lemon zest and the rest of the vanilla, then fold through the whites with the flour.Pile into three tall peaks in the dish with a spatula.Bake until golden outside and soft in the middle.Dust with icing sugar and serve at once.DrinksLiesl's gazebo elderflower fizzElderflower cordial, cloudy apple and lemon over ice with mint, topped with sodaHow to make it200ml elderflower cordial400ml cloudy apple juice3 lemons, 2 juiced and 1 sliced into wheels1 bunch mint4 cups ice1 L soda waterMix the elderflower cordial, apple juice and lemon juice in a jug.Bruise most of the mint and add to the jug.Fill 4 tall glasses with ice and pour in the elderflower mix.Top with soda water and stir gently.Garnish with a lemon wheel and a mint sprig.
